content.what_it_is: MATLAB script (Monai Valley spherical benchmark, fft/ directory) generating wavemaker components (period, amplitude, phase) from an input time series -- same algorithm as the Mase-Kirby fft4wavemaker.m but different inputs: reads time_ser_input.txt (L5) truncated to 1024 samples ('1*1024' L6); sample_frequency=0.5 (sampling interval 0.5 s, L7 and t=[0:N-1]*sample_frequency L16); band-pass low_cutoff_freq=0.001 / high_cutoff_freq=0.03333 Hz (L8-9, i.e. periods 30-1000 s, tsunami band); scale_fac=100.0 (L10, m to cm); output wavemk_per_amp_pha.txt (L11). FFT decomposition (L17-23: a0=d(1)/m, an=2*real(d(2:M))/m, bn=-2*imag(d(2:M))/m), DFT interpolant y (L31-36), amplitudes/phases cn/en (L38-41), band-pass selection into per/cnn/enn (L43-52), band-limited reconstruction z (L54-60). Plot compares data, interpolant, and approximation all scaled by scale_fac (L69-75). Output loop scales cnn by scale_fac (L80) and writes per/cnn/enn rows '%12.8f %12.8f %12.8f' (L82-85).
entities: script variables: data1 @L5, data @L6, sample_frequency @L7, low_cutoff_freq @L8, high_cutoff_freq @L9, scale_fac @L10, output_file @L11, nr,nc @L14, wave @L15, t @L16, d @L17, m @L18, M @L19, time @L20, a0 @L21, an @L22, bn @L23, n @L25, x @L26, y @L29, cn @L39, en @L40, icount @L43, ff @L45, per @L48, cnn @L49, enn @L50, z @L54, fid @L78
calls: clear all @L3; load @L5; size @L14; fft @L17; floor @L19; zeros @L29, @L54; sqrt @L39; atan2 @L40; clf @L69; plot @L70, @L72, @L74; legend @L75; fopen @L78; fprintf @L83; fclose @L85

verbatim_spans.text: data1=load('time_ser_input.txt'); % one- (ele) or two-column time series (t,ele)

unresolved: sample_frequency=0.5 (L7) is again the sampling interval, not a frequency (rate 2 Hz); variable name contradicts usage.
scale_fac=100.0 (L10) multiplies both plots and output amplitudes -- m-to-cm conversion consistent with the spherical runs' cm convention, but the input file's units are not stated.

L6 truncates to 1024 samples and linear-indexes data1, which would interleave a two-column input despite the L5 comment allowing (t,ele); L13 comment retains the non-ASCII encoding artifact; commented cutoff_number fprintf (L81) references an undefined variable.
